item.title: Networking
item.description:
Considerations of Peer-to-Peer Communication 🔗

When two people open the same design, their browsers exchange edits directly over WebRTC. Layer5 Cloud takes part only at the start and for presence. Edits do not pass through Layer5 Cloud or Meshery Server.

A self-hosted provider is its own signaling host. Browsers open a WebSocket to /collaboration on your deployment. Users connected to your deployment never signal through Layer5’s hosted service, and there is no public Layer5 signaling server to point them at.

item.title: Organization Configuration Scenarios
item.description:
Every organization in Layer5 Cloud is configured based on two simple choices: where your users sign in (your front door) and whose identity provider authenticates them. Those two choices combine into a small set of named scenarios. This guide names each one, describes what your users experience, and explains when you would choose one over the next.

For the step-by-step setup behind these choices, follow the links into White-labeling (themes, logos, custom domains) and Identity Services (bring-your-own-credentials and authentication boundaries). This page is the map; those are the turn-by-turn directions.

item.title: Identity and Security
item.description:
Organizations are the basic unit of multi-tenancy inside of Layer5 Cloud. The identity structure is flexible: an organization has any number of teams, a team has any number of members, and a user can belong to any number of teams and organizations.

Identity and security answer two questions for every request: who is acting, and what that person may do in the organization the request runs in. Organization membership, the roles a person holds in that organization, and resources shared with them directly each contribute. The same person can hold different access in each organization they belong to.

item.title: Identity Services
item.description:
Layer5 Cloud offers a built-in identity provider (IDP), supporting OIDC for normal users and token-based authentication (access, ID, refresh tokens) for API clients with JSON Web Signature (JWS) for token signing. Layer5 Cloud users can sign-up via email and password in addition to social identity providers (Google and GitHub) via OAuth2. See Getting Started with a Layer5 Account for details.

Layer5 Cloud identity services include account recovery, email verification, and social sign-in with Google and GitHub. Password sign-in is on, with a minimum of 8 characters, a check against known-breached passwords, and a rejection when the password is too similar to the account identifier.
